Wait, I see something interesting in `clear_meta_and_links`:
```python
    @lru_cache(maxsize=128)
    def clear_meta_and_links(self) -> "Style":

        style: Style = self.__new__(Style)

        style._hash = self._hash

```
The `style._hash = self._hash` line is copying the hash of the original style (which includes `_meta`) to the new style (which has `_meta = None`).
This means the new style will have the same hash as the original style, even though its `_meta` is different.
This is likely the bug. The hashed cache (the `_hash` attribute) is not being cleared when clearing meta.

If `_meta` is part of the hash calculation in `__hash__`:
```python
    def __hash__(self) -> int:
        if self._hash is not None:
            return self._hash
        self._hash = hash(
            (
                self._color,
                self._bgcolor,
                self._attributes,
                self._set_attributes,
                self._link,
                self._meta,
            )
        )
        return self._hash
```
Then when `clear_meta_and_links` creates a new style with `_meta = None`, it should not copy `self._hash` if `self._meta` was not `None`. Or more simply, it should set `style._hash = None` so that the hash is re-calculated when needed.

steps.message: The `submit_patch` call was successful. I have fixed the bug where `clear_meta_and_links` was incorrectly copying the hash of the original style, which led to incorrect hash values when metadata was removed. I verified the fix with a reproduction script.

The bug was located in `rich/style.py` within the `clear_meta_and_links` method. When creating a new `Style` object without metadata and links, the method was copying the `_hash` of the original style. Since the `Style.__hash__` implementation includes the `_meta` attribute in its calculation, the new style (which had `_meta = None`) incorrectly retained the hash of the original style.

I fixed this by changing `style._hash = self._hash` to `style._hash = None` in `rich/style.py`, which forces the hash to be recalculated the next time it is accessed. I verified the fix using a reproduction script that confirmed the hashes of a style and its "cleared" version are now different.
